Companies spend years learning how an employee performs, collaborates, recovers from mistakes, and navigates the business. When that person leaves, much of the useful record usually collapses into an exit form, a disabled email address, and somebody's memory.

The company announced the round on September 14, 2026, as it emerged from stealth with software for offboarding and corporate alumni management.

The broader bet is that former employees are becoming a more important source of trusted talent while the external hiring funnel becomes easier to flood and harder to verify. September 10, 2026

• Jesse Landry

# Botsi Raises $1.5M for AI Subscription Pricing

Botsi is moving subscription pricing from a periodic growth experiment into a live decision system. The New York company announced a $1.5M pre-seed round on September 9, 2026, from Telegraph Ventures, Plain Sight Capital, Atlanta Technology Angels, VentureSouth, and angel investors.

The company trains a custom model for each subscription app, then uses behavior and context to select a price, paywall, or offer for an individual user. Instead of asking which single paywall wins on average, Botsi asks which offer is most likely to fit the customer arriving now.

That distinction matters because subscription businesses live inside an awkward trade-off. A higher price can lift revenue per buyer while losing price-sensitive customers, and a lower price can preserve conversion while leaving money behind from customers who would have paid more. Botsi is financing the infrastructure to make many of those decisions at once, then measure whether they actually improve lifetime value.

# Dapta Raises $6M to Bring AI Agents to Non-English Businesses

 Nicolas Rojas 

CEO

## Built for the founders AI forgot

Behind millions of businesses in the US is a founder who thinks in another language.

The roofer in Houston. The family that runs a law firm in Miami. The insurance agent in Phoenix who built a book of business one referral at a time. Their customers might speak English, Spanish, or both. But the founder learns, decides and buys in their own language.

That matters more than anyone in AI has noticed. Business owners don’t adopt technology from a settings page. They adopt it from someone they trust, who explains it in the language they think in. Almost every AI platform is sold, taught and supported in English, so these founders get AI last, if they get it at all.

We think that’s the biggest opportunity in AI right now. And we’re winning it.

# Arzana's AI Agents Read RFQs and Write Quotes for US Manufacturers

The Y Combinator alum's software integrates with Epicor and NetSuite to handle repetitive paperwork, backed by a seed round led by Sunshine Lake VC.

By Pipe Haddad

About Arzana

Published 2026-10-13T00:27:09.026Z

The most expensive part of a manufacturing order isn't the raw material or the machine time. It's the 45 minutes a sales engineer spends reading a complex RFQ, pulling pricing from a legacy ERP, applying a dozen business rules and discounts, and manually generating a quote. That's the wedge Arzana is using to sell AI agents into the front offices of American factories.

Founded in 2025, Arzana sells what it calls an Office Execution System, a layer of software that sits on top of a manufacturer's existing email and ERP stack. Its agents are trained on a customer's own historical data to automate workflows like quoting, order entry, invoicing, and routine customer service.
